Single Bench:
 Hon. Shri Justice G.S. Ahluwalia
 Criminal Revision No.1782/1999
.........Applicant: Shivprasad Gupta
 Versus
.........Respondents: State of M.P. and another
Shri Shribhan Sahu, Counsel for the applicant.
Shri Yogesh Dhande, Public Prosecutor for respondent/State.

(16/11/2017) Per Justice G.S. Ahluwalia, This Criminal Revision under Sections 397, 401 of Cr.P.C.
has been filed against the judgment and sentence dated 29-11- 1999 passed by 3rd A.S.J., Rewa in Criminal Appeal No.5/1997 arising out of judgment and sentence dated 17-12-1996 passed by C.J.M., Rewa in Criminal Case No.684/1992 by which the applicant has been convicted under Section 7(1) read with Section 16(1)(a)(1) and Section 14 "A" read with Section 16 (1-C) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (In short "the Act) and sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment of 6 months and a fine of Rs.1,000/- and to undergo rigorous imprisonment of one month and a fine of Rs.500/-, respectively.

The necessary facts for the disposal of the present Criminal Revision in short are that on 26-5-1995,
the Food Inspector, S.P. 2 Criminal Revision No.1782/1999 [Shivprasad Gupta Vs. State of M.P. and another] Dubey inspected the shop of the applicant and purchased 3 packets of vermicelli from the shop of the applicant.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The packets were sealed on the spot and Panchnama was prepared.
Sample was sent to the Public Analyst.
The remaining two packets were deposited in the office of Local Health Authority.
The applicant did not produce any receipt of purchase of the packets of vermicelli and he also did not disclose the name of the shop from where he had purchased vermicelli.
The Public Analyst found the vermicelli adulterated.
The permission for prosecution was obtained and thereafter complaint was filed for prosecution.

sentences.text:
The Trial Court after recording evidence and considering the documentary evidence, convicted the applicant for offence under Section 7(1) read with Section 16(1)(a)(1) and Section 14 "A" read with Section 16 (1-C) of the Act and sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment of 6 months and a fine of Rs.1,000/- and to undergo rigorous imprisonment of one month and a fine of Rs.500/-,
respectively.

Being aggrieved by the judgment and sentence passed by the Trial Court, the applicant filed an appeal, which too suffered dismissal by Judgment dated 29-11-1999 passed by 3 rd A.S.J., Rewa in Criminal Appeal No.5/1997.
Challenging the conviction and sentence, it is submitted by the Counsel for the applicant that the Food Inspector had no authority and jurisdiction to take the samples.
The independent witnesses have not supported the prosecution case.
The report of the Public Analyst is vague.
The provisions of Section 11(1)(a), 11(4) of the Act have not been complied with.

The applicant was not supplied the copy of the report of Public Analyst as a result of which the applicant was deprived of his valuable right of getting the vermicelli re-examined by Central Food Laboratory.
It is further submitted that the present revision has not been disposed of within a reasonable time and

the delay in final disposal of this 3 Criminal Revision No.1782/1999 [Shivprasad Gupta Vs. State of M.P. and another]
revision has caused great difficulty as the applicant is now 52 years and in case if he is sent to jail,
then it would cause great hardship to the applicant.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Per contra, it is submitted by the Counsel for the State that the Food Inspector has been duly appointed by the State Govt. and he was appointed for the entire Division and he had collected the samples within his jurisdiction.
The applicant neither produced the receipt nor disclosed the name of the shop from where he had purchased the vermicelli, therefore, he is not protected.
The copy of the report of Public Analyst was supplied to the applicant and inspite of that, he did not exercise his right under Section 13(2) of the Act.
Heard the learned Counsel for the parties.
The applicant has raised a very important question of delay in disposal of the present revision.

The question is that whether the applicant himself was interested in early disposal of the present revision or he himself was interested in keeping the present revision pending so that he can enjoy the bail.
The order- sheets of this case reveal that this Court by order dated 6-12-1999 had granted bail.
Thereafter, the case was taken up for hearing on 15-12-2000, but none appeared on behalf of the applicant therefore, the case was adjourned.
Again the case was taken up for hearing on 25-3-2013, but none appeared for the applicant therefore, show cause notice was issued to the applicant as to why his bail may not be cancelled.

Thereafter the case was listed on 2-5-2013,17-6-2013, 5-7-2013, 11-11-2013, 5-12-2013, 5-12- 2016, 9-1-2017 and 27-2-2017, but hearing of the case was adjourned at the request of the Counsel for the applicant.

Thus, it is clear that in fact it was the applicant who was not interested in early disposal of the present revision and whenever the case was taken up for final hearing, the same was got adjourned on one pretext or the other.
It is a well established principle of law that a 4 Criminal Revision No.1782/1999 [Shivprasad Gupta Vs. State of M.P. and another] person cannot take advantage of his own wrong.

sentences.text: It is the contention of the applicant that the Food Inspector was not competent to take samples.
The Food Inspector was appointed on the post of Sanitary Inspector by order Ex. P.2 and he was appointed as Food Inspector by the State Govt. by notification dated 9-8-1991 Ex. P.4.
The applicant was appointed in Rewa Division by order dated 5-11-1981 Ex. P.6 and the Controller, Food and Medicine Department, by order dated 20-7- 1988.
The Food Inspectors posted in District Flying Squad, were authorized to act as food Inspector in their entire Revenue Division.
The applicant was posted in Rewa, therefore, he was competent to exercise his power in the entire Rewa Revenue Division.
It is not the case of the applicant that the shop of the applicant was not situated within the Revenue Division of Rewa.
Thus, it is held that the Food Inspector was competent to take samples and he had acted within his jurisdiction.
It is next contended by the Counsel for the applicant that he had purchased the vermicelli from the market and since he is not the manufacturer, therefore, he is protected.

The submission made by the Counsel for the applicant cannot be accepted for the simple reason that the S.P. Dubey (P.W.1) has stated in his examination-in-chief that the applicant was asked to produce the receipt of purchase of vermicelli, but he did not produce the same.
He also did not disclose the name of seller.
Even during the trial, the applicant has not produced any receipt to show that from where he had purchased the vermicelli.
Under this circumstance, it cannot be held that the applicant was not the manufacturer or was entitled for protection.

As the applicant did not produce the 5 Criminal Revision No.1782/1999 [Shivprasad Gupta Vs. State of M.P. and another] receipt of purchase of vermicelli, as well as did not disclose the name of the seller, therefore, it cannot be said that there was any warranty in favor of the applicant.

entities.text: 5 Criminal Revision No.1782/1999 [Shivprasad Gupta Vs. State of M.P. and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, the applicant is not entitled for protection under Section 14 of Act.
Even the applicant did not disclose the name of the vendor as required under Section 14-A of the Act.

It is next contended by the Counsel for the applicant that the copy of the report of the Public Analyst was not sent and hence, he has been deprived of his valuable right of re-examination of the sample by Central Food Laboratory.
The contention made by the Counsel for the applicant is misconceived and is hereby rejected.
S.P. Dubey (P.W.1) has specifically stated that after filing the complaint, a copy of the report of the Public Analyst was sent to the applicant by registered post on 15-5-1996 Ex. P.20.
Where a document is sent by a registered post, then a presumption can be drawn under Section 27 of General Clauses Act that the said letter must have been delivered to the applicant.
It is also clear from the record that the applicant did not exercise his right under Section 13(2) of the Act.

It is further submitted by the Counsel for the applicant that since the independent witnesses did not support the prosecution story, therefore, the solitary evidence of S.P. Dubey (P.W.1) is not reliable.

The submission made by the Counsel for the applicant cannot be accepted merely on the ground that unless and until it is proved by the applicant that the Food Inspector was an interested witness,

sentences.text: his evidence cannot be rejected merely on the ground that he is a departmental witness.
No further argument was advanced by the Counsel for the applicant.
No perversity could be pointed out by the Counsel for the applicant to show that findings of facts recorded by the Courts below warrant interference.

Considering the oral evidence as well as the documentary 6 Criminal Revision No.1782/1999 [Shivprasad Gupta Vs. State of M.P. and another] evidence, this Court is of the considered opinion that the prosecution has succeeded in establishing beyond reasonable doubt that the vermicelli, the samples of which were taken from the shop of the applicant, were adulterated and the applicant has failed to prove that he had purchased the vermicelli from any shop.

sentences.text: Accordingly, he is held guilty under Section 7(1) read with Section 16(1)(a)(i) and Section 14 "A" read with Section 16 (1-C) of the Act.
The Trial Court has awarded sentence of six months' rigorous imprisonment and a fine of Rs.1,000/- and one month's rigorous imprisonment and a fine of Rs.500/-, respectively.
Since, the minimum sentence has been awarded by the Trial Court, therefore, the sentence awarded by the Courts below does not call for any interference.

Accordingly, the judgment and sentence dated 29-11-1999 passed by 3rd A.S.J., Rewa in Criminal Appeal No.5/1997 arising out of judgment and sentence dated 17-12-1996 passed by C.J.M. Rewa in Criminal Case No.684/1992 are hereby affirmed.
The applicant is on bail.
His bail bonds and surety bonds are hereby cancelled.
He is directed to immediately surrender before the Trial Court for undergoing the remaining jail sentence.
The revision fails and is hereby dismissed.
(G.S. Ahluwalia) Judge Arun* 7 Criminal Revision No.1782/1999 [Shivprasad Gupta Vs. State of M.P. and another] 16/11/2017
